---
title: SvelteKit, Remix, Bun, Deno and Workers
description: Wire the ClipMux handler into any framework or runtime that speaks Fetch requests and responses.
---

`clipmuxHandler` is a Fetch handler: a function from `Request` to
`Response`, using only Web APIs. Any framework or runtime that hands you a
`Request` can run it. Each section below is the whole wiring; the
callbacks are the same everywhere.

## Before you start

- The packages, and your app connected with `init`, which writes the
  `CLIPMUX_*` settings to `.env.local`:

<Tabs items={['npm', 'pnpm']}>
<Tab value="npm">

```bash
npm i @clipmux/node @clipmux/uploader @clipmux/player
npx @clipmux/node init --server https://video.example.com
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="pnpm">

```bash
pnpm add @clipmux/node @clipmux/uploader @clipmux/player
pnpm dlx @clipmux/node init --server https://video.example.com
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

- Your callbacks. Every example below imports them from a module of your
  own, `$lib/clipmux` or `./clipmux`:

```ts title="clipmux.ts"
import type { HandlerOptions } from '@clipmux/node/handlers'

export const callbacks: HandlerOptions = {
  async upload(req, { file }) {
    const user = await requireInstructor(req)
    const lesson = new URL(req.url).searchParams.get('lesson')
    return { passthrough: `lesson_${lesson}`, title: file.name, generate: { subtitles: true } }
  },
  async playback(req, { playbackId }) {
    const user = await getUser(req)
    return (await canWatch(user, playbackId)) ? { viewerId: user.id } : null
  },
  async asset(asset) {
    await db.lesson.update({
      where: { ref: asset.passthrough },
      data: { status: asset.status, playbackId: asset.playback_ids[0]?.id },
    })
  },
}
```

`requireInstructor`, `getUser`, `canWatch` and `db` stand for your own code.

The handler picks its route from the last part of the URL path, `upload`,
`playback` or `webhook`, and answers only POST. Mount it so those three
paths reach it, and let it read the request body itself: the webhook's
signature covers the raw body.

## SvelteKit

```ts title="src/routes/api/clipmux/[action]/+server.ts"
import { ClipMux } from '@clipmux/node'
import { clipmuxHandler } from '@clipmux/node/handlers'
import { env } from '$env/dynamic/private'
import type { RequestHandler } from './$types'
import { callbacks } from '$lib/clipmux'

const clipmux = clipmuxHandler({ ...callbacks, clipmux: new ClipMux({ env }) })

export const POST: RequestHandler = ({ request }) => clipmux(request)
```

`$env/dynamic/private` gives the client the server's environment in
development and on every adapter, and never reaches the browser. In
development, SvelteKit reads `.env` and `.env.local`.

## Remix

```ts title="app/routes/api.clipmux.$action.ts"
import { clipmuxHandler } from '@clipmux/node/handlers'
import type { ActionFunctionArgs } from '@remix-run/node'
import { callbacks } from '~/clipmux'

const clipmux = clipmuxHandler(callbacks)

export const action = ({ request }: ActionFunctionArgs) => clipmux(request)
```

`new ClipMux()` reads `process.env`. Make sure the `CLIPMUX_*` settings are
there in development too, for example by starting the dev server with
`node --env-file=.env.local` or loading the file with dotenv.

## Bun

```ts title="server.ts"
import { clipmuxHandler } from '@clipmux/node/handlers'
import { callbacks } from './clipmux'

const clipmux = clipmuxHandler(callbacks)

Bun.serve({
  port: 3000,
  fetch(req) {
    if (new URL(req.url).pathname.startsWith('/api/clipmux/')) return clipmux(req)
    return new Response('Not found', { status: 404 })
  },
})
```

Bun loads `.env.local` into `process.env` by itself.

## Deno

```ts title="server.ts"
import { ClipMux } from '@clipmux/node'
import { clipmuxHandler } from '@clipmux/node/handlers'
import { callbacks } from './clipmux.ts'

const clipmux = clipmuxHandler({ ...callbacks, clipmux: new ClipMux({ env: Deno.env.toObject() }) })

Deno.serve({ port: 3000 }, (req) => {
  if (new URL(req.url).pathname.startsWith('/api/clipmux/')) return clipmux(req)
  return new Response('Not found', { status: 404 })
})
```

Passing `env` hands the client its settings directly. Run it with
`deno run --allow-net --allow-env --env-file=.env.local server.ts`. Install
the packages with npm as above, or import them with the `npm:` prefix
(`npm:@clipmux/node`).

## Cloudflare Workers

Workers have no `process.env`; their settings arrive as `env` with each
request. Give the handler a client built from it:

```ts title="src/index.ts"
import { ClipMux } from '@clipmux/node'
import { clipmuxHandler } from '@clipmux/node/handlers'
import { callbacks } from './clipmux'

export default {
  fetch: (req: Request, env: Record<string, string>) =>
    clipmuxHandler({ ...callbacks, clipmux: new ClipMux({ env }) })(req),
}
```

Set the five `CLIPMUX_*` values as secrets of the Worker, for example with
`wrangler secret put CLIPMUX_API_KEY`, rather than in `wrangler.toml`. Route
only `/api/clipmux/*` to this code if the Worker serves other paths too.

## Add the elements

In your pages, load the two elements and point them at the route:

```html
<script type="module">
  import '@clipmux/uploader/element'
  import '@clipmux/player/element'
</script>
<clipmux-uploader create-url="/api/clipmux/upload?lesson=42"></clipmux-uploader>
<clipmux-player playback-id="pid_…" session-url="/api/clipmux/playback"></clipmux-player>
```

In a server-rendered framework, load the elements in the browser only:
in SvelteKit from `onMount`, in Remix from `useEffect`, as in
[Add the player](/docs/build/play/player).

## Check it works

```bash
npx @clipmux/node doctor
npx @clipmux/node listen --forward-to localhost:3000/api/clipmux/webhook
```

Use your app's port. `doctor` ends with `✓ Ready.` Upload a file from your
page; when it's encoded, `listen` prints `✓ video.asset.ready ast_… → 200`.

- `500` from the handler, with a `ClipMuxConfigError` in your logs naming a
  variable: the settings didn't reach the client. On SvelteKit, Workers and
  Deno, check you passed `clipmux: new ClipMux({ env })`.
- `400` in `listen`: the secret is wrong, or something read the body first.
